content:
Laptop manufacturers were already trigger-happy shipping a boatload of machines with a ton of bloatware that would require ample time to remove. Even now, a fresh copy of Windows 11 arrives with a plethora of unwanted software, and it appears that the situation will worsen with time.
Lenovo, the world’s largest PC manufacturer, has reportedly begun pre-installing the desktop version of ChatGPT on select new Windows 11 business notebooks, signaling a new wave of third-party AI software bundling on commercial hardware. To make the offer salivating for business operators, an OpenAI promotion offers corporate buyers up to $100 per seat in workspace credits.
The proliferation of ChatGPT running on business laptops has begun, as business owners will gladly accept OpenAI’s $100 credit and potentially save millions
Details uncovered in an OpenAI support document by Windows Latest confirm that the promotional credits are strictly tied to eligible Lenovo devices that ship with ChatGPT pre-installed from the factory. Businesses with an existing ChatGPT Business workspace can claim a one-time $100 credit toward their shared workspace balance simply by signing in through the pre-installed client.
Companies that create a new Business workspace through the offer will reportedly receive a substantially larger incentive. However, as you’d expect, the promotion arrives with certain hurdles. For instance, you can avail two credit tiers, as the funds are deposited into the workspace’s shared balance with a 60-day expiration window.
It should also be mentioned that the offer can only be availed through the pre-installed ChatGPT app. OpenAI says to “Look for ChatGPT in Start. You may also see it in Lenovo Now or Lenovo Vantage. Contact Lenovo if you’re unsure whether ChatGPT came preinstalled on your device.”
![](https://cdn.wccftech.com/files/placeholder-mobile.png)
![](https://cdn.wccftech.com/files/placeholder-desktop.png)
Lenovo is following the same approach as Microsoft, with the latter bundling Copilot natively into Windows 11. The Chinese PC manufacturer will soon expand its AI partnership across consumer product lines such as Yoga and Legion, meaning one additional program that users have to uninstall if they prefer using competitors’ solutions such as Claude or Gemini. In any case, if businesses are willing to save millions over these $100 credits, then there’s no question that AI bloatware will be prevalent in even more laptop brands.
Assuming more of these programs will start being bundled with Lenovo’s laptops, the company should at least take a back seat in pre-installing its other bloatware, as it consumes unnecessary storage and resources. There’s also a possibility that these unwanted programs could be wearing down the SSD when running as background tasks, but there’s no way to confirm this behavior, at least for now.
